Requirement: Where screen or video capture is enabled, the system shall require explicit per-session activation or an administrator-approved rule.
The system shall display separate indicators for audio, screen, and camera capture.
The system shall preserve audio-video synchronization and link transcript timestamps to video playback.
The system shall allow users to create a clip by selecting transcript text, timestamps, or an extracted outcome.
When a clip is created, the system shall preserve source provenance and allow redaction before export or sharing.
The system shall calculate talk-time by identified speaker and disclose how silence, overlap, and unassigned speech are handled.
The system shall calculate configurable meeting metrics including questions, interruptions, speaking pace, topic duration, and action-item closure.
Every calculated metric shall link to underlying segments or disclose the calculation method.
The system shall allow users to disable individual analytics and coaching categories.
The system shall provide sales coaching focused on objections, questions, next steps, and evidence-backed follow-up.
The system shall provide interview assistance focused on questions asked, candidate evidence, follow-ups, and rubric coverage without inferring protected traits.
The system shall provide facilitation coaching focused on participation balance, unresolved decisions, and agenda coverage.
The system shall provide presentation coaching focused on pace, filler words, question handling, and audience interaction.
The system shall not assign personality, emotion, honesty, health, or protected-class labels from voice or video.
The system shall generate recurring trend reports for approved projects, clients, teams, topics, objections, risks, requests, and decisions.
When a trend report cites a change, the system shall link to the meetings and evidence that support the change.
The system shall compare selected meetings and identify consistent, changed, resolved, and contradictory items.
The system shall generate a next-meeting agenda from open tasks, unresolved questions, previous agenda coverage, and recent decisions.

The system shall support expiring, access-controlled share links only through an explicitly configured self-hosted private deployment.
When a share link is created, the system shall allow expiration, password, download, watermark, and view-scope controls.
The system shall record share-link creation, access, change, and revocation events.
The system shall allow users to revoke a share link immediately.
The system shall capture microphone and system audio through platform-specific adapters that implement a common capture contract.
When recording begins, the system shall create separate synchronized microphone and system-audio tracks when both sources are available.
Where multitrack capture is unsupported, the system shall disclose the limitation and preserve source attribution to the greatest supported extent.
The system shall create a mixed playback track without destroying the original synchronized source tracks.
The system shall timestamp captured frames using a monotonic clock suitable for cross-track alignment.
If microphone and system tracks drift beyond the configured tolerance, the system shall correct or flag the drift without truncating content.
When the active audio device changes, the system shall offer to switch devices and shall preserve the existing meeting timeline.
If an active audio device disconnects, the system shall continue capturing available sources and display a recoverable warning.
The system shall allow the user to select microphone, system source, sample rate profile, and optional noise controls before recording.
The system shall provide a live input meter for each enabled source.
If clipping is detected, the system shall warn the user and provide an actionable gain recommendation where platform controls allow it.
If prolonged silence is detected after recording starts, the system shall ask whether the intended sources are selected without stopping automatically.
The system shall support manual start, pause, resume, stop, and privacy-pause controls through the main window and configurable global shortcuts.
When capture is paused, the system shall preserve timeline continuity and mark the paused interval in meeting metadata.
When recording is stopped, the system shall finalize playable media before starting nonessential post-processing.
The system shall write media incrementally so an unexpected process termination does not discard the complete meeting.
When the application restarts after an interrupted recording, the system shall detect recoverable sessions and offer repair before normal library use.
If session repair cannot recover a complete container, the system shall preserve recoverable raw segments and provide a diagnostic explanation.
The system shall journal capture state, source configuration, and media segment checksums during recording.
If free disk space falls below the warning threshold, the system shall warn the user and estimate remaining safe recording time.
If free disk space falls below the stop threshold, the system shall finalize the current media segment and stop safely rather than corrupt the recording.
The system shall provide a Record Only mode that disables live transcription and summarization.
Where Deferred Processing mode is enabled, the system shall enqueue transcription after recording and show the pending state.
The system shall allow users to add timestamped markers and notes during recording without interrupting capture.
When a supported conferencing application starts a call, the system shall detect the event and display the configured recording prompt.
Where automatic recording is enabled for an application, the system shall start capture after the configured consent and countdown behavior.
When a detected call ends, the system shall stop capture after a configurable grace period unless the user elects to continue.
If multiple supported meeting applications are active, the system shall ask the user to select the intended source context or record a clearly labeled combined session.
The system shall allow per-application enablement, exclusion, auto-start, and auto-stop preferences.
The system shall support manual meeting mode for unsupported applications and in-person sessions.
When calendar access is authorized, the system shall use meeting title, time, link, attendees, and organizer as suggested metadata without joining the call.
If calendar and detected-call metadata conflict, the system shall show the ambiguity and allow the user to select the correct event.
The system shall not send a meeting bot or join a conference unless a separately enabled future feature explicitly requires it.
The system shall detect consecutive recordings with overlapping context and suggest merging them.
When the user merges recordings, the system shall preserve original media and a reversible merge history until the user confirms permanent consolidation.
The system shall allow capture-source attribution to be preserved through transcription, export, and reprocessing.
The system shall expose capture health including active sources, dropped-frame count, buffer pressure, disk state, and processing lag in an optional diagnostics view.
While recording, the system shall prioritize uninterrupted media persistence over live transcription, indexing, animations, or nonessential network activity.
If system load threatens audio continuity, the system shall degrade or pause nonessential processing and inform the user after capture is safe.
The system shall pass a continuous 24-hour capture soak test on each supported desktop platform.
The system shall preserve an audit event for recording start, pause, resume, privacy pause, source change, and stop.
Where optional screen or video capture is enabled, the system shall require a separate explicit activation and display a distinct active-capture indicator.
The system shall export transcripts in TXT, Markdown, VTT, SRT, and versioned JSON formats.
The system shall export summaries and structured outcomes in Markdown, HTML, PDF, DOCX, and versioned JSON formats where supported.
The system shall export action items and decisions in CSV and versioned JSON formats.
The system shall create a portable meeting bundle containing selected media, transcripts, artifacts, metadata, checksums, and a manifest.
When a meeting bundle is imported, the system shall validate schema compatibility and checksums before adding content to the library.
If an imported bundle uses a newer unsupported schema, the system shall preserve the file and explain the compatibility limitation.
The system shall allow users to choose whether exports include speaker profiles, local model provenance, revision history, and private notes.
The system shall preserve timestamps, speaker labels, evidence links, and relationships in machine-readable exports.
The system shall provide a generic outbound webhook for meeting-created, meeting-completed, artifact-approved, task-updated, and export-ready events.
The system shall sign webhook payloads with a workspace-specific secret.
The system shall include an idempotency key and schema version in every webhook delivery.
If a webhook delivery fails, the system shall retry using a bounded backoff policy and expose the next retry time.
If a webhook returns a permanent failure, the system shall stop automatic retries and request user intervention.
The system shall provide a webhook test function that shows the exact payload and response without requiring a real meeting.
The system shall provide an approval queue for every outbound message, task, document, CRM note, calendar action, webhook, and share action.
Where automatic sending is enabled, the system shall restrict automation to approved templates, destinations, scopes, fields, and conditions and shall never send raw meeting content by default.
The system shall display exactly which meeting fields will leave the device, the destination, and the purpose before a user approves an outbound action.
The system shall allow users to revoke connector credentials and cancel queued jobs for that connector.
The system shall store connector credentials in a protected secrets store.
The system shall provide connector health, token expiry, permission scope, last success, last failure, and remediation guidance.
The system shall support sending approved meeting notes and follow-ups to Slack and Microsoft Teams.
The system shall support publishing approved artifacts to Notion, Google Docs, and Microsoft OneNote.
The system shall support creating and updating tasks in Jira, Linear, and Asana.
The system shall support creating approved meeting notes, contacts, activities, and follow-ups in HubSpot and Salesforce.
When an external task is created, the system shall store the external identifier and destination link.
Where bidirectional task sync is enabled, the system shall reconcile supported status changes without duplicating the task.
If an external record was modified outside Menie, the system shall show the conflict before overwriting supported fields.
The system shall support calendar event creation and agenda attachment for approved follow-up meetings.
The system shall allow routing rules based on template, project, participant, tag, meeting source, and approved artifact type.
The system shall allow users to disable an automation rule without deleting its configuration or history.
The system shall provide an automation run history including trigger, input scope, approval, destination, result, retries, and actor.
The system shall publish a versioned connector SDK with authentication, schema, error, retry, and privacy requirements.
A third-party connector shall pass conformance tests before it can be marked verified.
The system shall provide documented n8n workflow examples for common meeting-completion and action-item flows.
The system shall prevent connector code from accessing meetings or fields outside its approved scope and shall isolate connectors from local model prompts, embeddings, and unrelated artifacts.
The system shall allow export and connector actions to be disabled by administrator policy.
The system shall allow users to redact selected transcript text or media regions before export or sharing.
When redaction is applied to a delivered artifact, the system shall exclude recoverable original content from the exported copy.
The system shall provide a chat interface scoped to the active meeting.
When answering a meeting-scoped question, the system shall cite transcript timestamps or artifact evidence used in the answer.
The system shall provide Chat with History across user-selected projects, folders, participants, tags, and date ranges.
Before a cross-meeting query is executed, the system shall display the active knowledge scope.
The system shall generate embeddings, retrieve evidence, and generate answers locally using approved embedded models.
The system shall display the active local embedding model, local Gemma profile, indexed scope, expected resource use, and 100% Local AI state before indexing or answering.
The system shall index transcript chunks, meeting metadata, decisions, tasks, risks, and approved artifacts.
The system shall exclude trashed, expired, access-restricted, or explicitly excluded content from retrieval.
When a meeting changes, the system shall update only affected index entries rather than rebuilding the complete index.
When an embedding model changes, the system shall support a resumable re-index and preserve the old index until the new index is verified.
The system shall support hybrid retrieval using keyword, vector, metadata, recency, and entity signals.
The system shall provide direct answer, chronology, comparison, decision history, task status, and evidence-list answer modes.
When evidence is insufficient, the system shall state that it cannot answer reliably and show the closest available sources.
The system shall not fabricate a meeting, speaker, decision, task, date, or quote absent from retrieved evidence.
The system shall allow users to open every cited source in its original meeting context.
The system shall allow users to exclude a meeting or project from knowledge indexing.
The system shall allow users to delete and rebuild indexes without deleting source meetings.
The system shall provide local index health including embedding model, version, coverage, queue state, errors, disk usage, and no-egress verification state.
If indexing fails for one meeting, the system shall continue indexing other eligible meetings and surface the failed item.
The system shall allow users to export and import compatible local indexes with model and schema metadata.
The system shall apply workspace and object permissions before retrieval, generation, citation display, and export.
The system shall apply retention and legal-hold policies to knowledge indexes.
The system shall protect against prompt instructions embedded in transcript content by treating retrieved meeting text as untrusted data.
The system shall separate system instructions, user query, retrieved evidence, and tool output in the generation pipeline.
The system shall provide a local evaluation harness for retrieval relevance, citation correctness, answer groundedness, and refusal behavior.
The system shall log local model, prompt, retrieval, and citation provenance for each answer while respecting privacy and retention settings.
The system shall support follow-up questions that retain the selected knowledge scope and cited conversation context.
When the user changes knowledge scope, the system shall clearly reset or annotate prior conversational assumptions.
The system shall allow an answer to be converted into a note, task, decision review, agenda item, or export draft.
The system shall meet profile-specific response-latency and memory targets for local queries on reference hardware and provide progress for longer operations.
The system shall provide a meeting library with list, compact, and timeline views.
The system shall allow meetings to be organized by folder, project, client, tag, participant, and custom saved view.
The system shall allow one meeting to belong to multiple tags and one primary project.
The system shall provide full-text search across meeting titles, transcript text, summaries, decisions, tasks, risks, notes, and tags.
The system shall support filters by date, participant, speaker, source application, project, language, status, and processing state.

The system shall allow users to save and name a search and filter combination.
The system shall provide default views for Needs Review, Failed Processing, Open Actions, Unassigned Actions, Unsent Follow-ups, and Recently Recorded.
The system shall allow meetings to be pinned, archived, restored, or moved to trash.

The system shall support bulk tagging, project assignment, archive, export, reprocess, delete, and retention changes.

If a bulk operation is interrupted, the system shall resume from the last completed item without duplicating work.
The system shall allow users to merge consecutive meetings and preserve the source-meeting lineage.

The system shall detect likely duplicate imports using checksums, duration, and metadata.

The system shall allow the user to change the meeting storage location through the UI.

The system shall provide local backup schedules and manual backup controls.

The system shall allow restoration into a new library for validation before replacing an existing library.
The system shall provide project dashboards showing chronology, recent decisions, open tasks, risks, participants, and unresolved questions.
The system shall allow users to define custom meeting statuses and status-based views.
The system shall support keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels throughout the library and search experience.
The system shall meet the defined search latency target with at least 100,000 transcript segments on reference hardware.
The system shall provide a storage-usage view by media, transcript, model, index, cache, trash, and backup.
When storage cleanup is requested, the system shall preview recoverable space and affected content before deletion.
The system shall provide iOS and Android applications capable of reliable in-person audio recording.

The mobile application shall write encrypted media incrementally during recording.
If the mobile application is interrupted, the system shall recover the partial session on next launch.

The mobile application shall support start, pause, resume, marker, privacy pause, and stop from supported lock-screen or notification controls.
The mobile application shall warn the user about battery, thermal, storage, microphone, Bluetooth, and background-execution conditions that threaten capture.
If a phone call or higher-priority audio session interrupts recording, the mobile application shall preserve the current file and clearly report the interruption.

Where on-device processing is unavailable or disabled, the system shall support encrypted transfer for deferred processing on a paired desktop Menie installation; no cloud AI fallback shall be offered.
The system shall support encrypted QR-based pairing between mobile and desktop devices.
When transferring a recording over the local network, the system shall verify integrity before marking the transfer complete.
If a transferred recording already exists, the system shall prevent duplicate import and offer merge or keep-both options.
The system shall support optional encrypted peer-to-peer or self-hosted synchronization across authorized devices.
The mobile application shall support voice memo and audio-file import.
The mobile application shall allow users to attach timestamped photos, whiteboards, and notes to a meeting.
The mobile application shall allow project, tag, template, language, and consent-state selection before or after recording.
The mobile application shall function in offline local-only mode without requiring an account.

The system shall provide a guided first-run flow that explains permissions, audio sources, the strict local-only AI boundary, the hardware benchmark, three Gemma profiles, storage, and privacy in plain language.
When the application is launched for the first time, the system shall prevent recording until the user has completed or explicitly skipped the capture-permission test.
When the user grants microphone permission, the system shall immediately verify that audio samples can be received and display an input-level indicator.
When the user enables system-audio capture, the system shall play or request a test sound and verify that the selected system source is capturable.
If an operating-system permission is denied, the system shall identify the denied permission and provide platform-specific steps to correct it.

After the hardware assessment, the system shall present exactly three local summary profiles: Efficient using Gemma 4 E2B IT Q4, Balanced using Gemma 4 E4B IT Q4, and High Accuracy using Gemma 4 12B IT Q4.

For each local Gemma profile, the system shall display model size, expected free-memory demand, disk size, relative summary quality, expected speed, battery and thermal impact, recommended meeting complexity, and confirmation that inference remains local.

When requested during installation or Settings, the system shall assess CPU, GPU, NPU where available, installed and currently available memory, free disk space, power state, and local inference throughput without uploading benchmark data.

When the hardware assessment completes, the system shall mark exactly one Gemma profile as Recommended and provide a concise device-specific justification based on the measured constraints and expected user experience.

When the user selects a non-recommended profile, the system shall allow the override, explain the likely speed, quality, memory, battery, or thermal consequences, and suggest Record Only or deferred summarization if capture reliability could be affected.

The system shall maintain an offline model catalog containing local model name, version, checksum, license, source, quantization, disk size, approximate load memory, supported hardware backends, context capacity, and product profile.
When a model is downloaded, the system shall verify its checksum before making it available for use.
If model verification fails, the system shall quarantine the downloaded file and offer a retry without activating the model.
When a newer compatible local model package is available, the system shall notify the user without changing the active model automatically unless signed model updates are enabled.
Where automatic model updates are enabled, the system shall retain the previously working model until the new model passes a local health check.
When a user removes a model, the system shall identify meetings or queued jobs that depend on the model and require confirmation before removal.
The system shall allow models and application data to be stored on user-selected supported locations.
If a selected storage location becomes unavailable, the system shall preserve metadata, prevent destructive writes, and guide the user to reconnect or relocate the library.
The system shall provide a sample meeting that can validate transcription, summarization, evidence links, and export without recording a real conversation.

When onboarding is complete, the system shall display a readiness checklist for audio, available memory, hardware acceleration, storage, selected Gemma profile, local inference health, and 100% Local AI status.
The system shall allow users to rerun onboarding tests from Settings at any time.
The system shall use consistent product, repository, release, documentation, and support links across installers, the application, and generated artifacts.
When an application update changes permissions, models, or data processing, the system shall present a focused migration explanation before the affected capability is used.
The system shall provide keyboard-accessible onboarding and expose meaningful labels to assistive technologies.
The system shall generate meeting artifacts from a versioned structured schema rather than storing only unstructured summary text.
The system shall provide default artifact sections for overview, decisions, action items, risks, blockers, unanswered questions, and next agenda.
When an action item is extracted, the system shall store description, owner, due date, status, confidence, and evidence links when available.
If an action item has no identifiable owner, the system shall label the owner as unassigned and surface it for review.
If a due date is implied but ambiguous, the system shall preserve the source phrase and request user confirmation instead of inventing a date.
When a decision is extracted, the system shall store the decision, status, rationale, participants, and supporting evidence when available.
The system shall distinguish confirmed decisions, proposals, questions, and unresolved options.
Every extracted decision, task, risk, blocker, and key claim shall link to one or more transcript timestamps or state that supporting evidence was not found.
When the user selects an evidence link, the system shall open the relevant transcript segment and media timestamp.
The system shall record local Gemma model, quantization, runtime, template, prompt version, transcript version, context configuration, and generation timestamp for every artifact.
The system shall provide default templates for General, Sales, Interview, Project, Research, Legal, Healthcare, and Lecture meetings.
The system shall allow users to create, duplicate, import, export, and version custom templates.
A custom template shall define required sections, instructions, output schema, language, evidence policy, and optional routing rules.
If a custom template produces invalid structured output, the system shall retain the raw response, report validation errors, and offer repair or regeneration.
The system shall allow users to regenerate one artifact section without overwriting other sections.
When a user has edited an artifact, the system shall not overwrite the edit during regeneration without explicit confirmation.
The system shall maintain artifact revision history and allow users to restore a previous version.
The system shall allow transcript, summary, tasks, decisions, risks, and follow-up drafts to be edited in the application.
The system shall provide undo and redo for editing actions within a meeting session.
The system shall allow users to mark extracted outcomes as approved, rejected, corrected, or needing review.
When a meeting contains contradictory statements or decisions, the system shall surface the conflict with evidence rather than silently selecting one.
When the same action item appears multiple times, the system shall suggest a consolidated item while preserving all evidence links.
The system shall generate an email follow-up draft from approved meeting outcomes.
The system shall generate a concise Slack or Teams update from approved meeting outcomes.
The system shall generate a next-meeting agenda using unresolved items, open actions, and recent decisions.
The system shall allow output language to be configured globally, per template, and per meeting.
The system shall allow the user to select a tone and length for follow-up drafts without changing the factual outcome data.
If a generated artifact contains content not supported by the transcript, the system shall allow the user to flag it as unsupported and include the case in local quality feedback.
The system shall provide a completion checklist showing unassigned tasks, ambiguous dates, unsupported claims, failed artifacts, and unsent follow-ups.
When all required review items are resolved, the system shall allow the user to mark the meeting as complete.
The system shall expose structured artifact data through local exports and the permissioned connector interface.
The system shall support organization-approved template libraries in team deployments.
Where a template is locked by policy, the system shall prevent unauthorized modification while allowing permitted per-meeting fields.

The system shall evaluate summary and extraction quality, latency, memory use, and no-egress behavior against a versioned test corpus before promoting a local model, prompt, template, or runtime change.
The system shall display a persistent 100% Local AI indicator for each active meeting, generated artifact, indexing job, and meeting-chat session.
The system shall process capture, transcription, diarization, summarization, embeddings, retrieval, and meeting chat on user-controlled hardware and label the state as 100% Local AI.
The system shall not send raw audio, video, transcript text, prompts, embeddings, retrieved evidence, or generated meeting intelligence to an external AI provider.

Where an optional outbound integration is enabled, the system shall distinguish that integration from AI processing and preview the exact approved fields, destination, and purpose before transmission.
If an optional integration would transmit a broader payload than previously approved, the system shall pause the job and obtain new approval before transmission.
The system shall default usage analytics and content telemetry to disabled.
Where analytics are enabled, the system shall provide a data inventory and allow the user to disable analytics without affecting core recording.

The system shall not include raw audio, transcript text, participant names, meeting titles, local model prompts, embeddings, or connector secrets in telemetry unless the user explicitly attaches reviewed files to a support report.
When the user creates a diagnostic bundle, the system shall preview included files and redact secrets by default.
The system shall store optional connector and self-hosted synchronization credentials using the operating system credential store or an equivalently protected secrets mechanism.
The system shall encrypt sensitive local meeting data at rest where the user or administrator enables library encryption.
Where library encryption is enabled, the system shall require an authenticated unlock method before exposing meeting content.
If encryption keys are unavailable, the system shall not silently create an unencrypted replacement library.
The system shall provide clear controls to delete a meeting, its media, transcript, artifacts, local index entries, speaker profiles where selected, and integration payloads under Menie control.
When a meeting is deleted, the system shall remove it from full-text and vector indexes within the configured deletion service level.
Where a trash period is configured, the system shall explain that content remains recoverable until the trash period expires.
When secure deletion is requested and supported by the storage medium, the system shall perform the configured deletion procedure and record the result.
The system shall allow users to export a machine-readable inventory of stored meetings, media, transcripts, artifacts, and indexes.
The system shall present a recording-consent reminder that can be configured by jurisdiction, organization, or user preference.
Where an audible consent notice is enabled, the system shall play the notice before normal capture begins and record that the notice was played.
Where visual consent acknowledgment is enabled, the system shall store the user-entered acknowledgment with the meeting metadata.
The system shall display an unambiguous recording indicator while any audio or video capture is active.
When the user activates Privacy Pause, the system shall stop persisting audio and transcript content until capture is resumed.

The system shall enforce local-only AI processing and allow administrators to restrict optional connectors, exports, sharing modes, model imports, and synchronization destinations.
If a policy prohibits an optional connector, export, share, model import, or synchronization destination, the system shall block the action and identify affected queued jobs.
The system shall record local model, quantization, runtime version, template, prompt version, transcript version, context settings, and generation configuration for every artifact.
The system shall provide data-retention rules by workspace, project, meeting type, and artifact class.
Where a legal hold applies, the system shall prevent deletion by unauthorized users and record attempted deletion events.

The system shall provide a privacy report that summarizes local models, storage locations, network egress policy, retention rules, optional integrations, synchronization, telemetry, encryption, and no-egress test status.
The system shall isolate capture from failures in transcription, summarization, indexing, integrations, and UI rendering.
The system shall implement idempotent processing jobs with durable state, retries, cancellation, and resumability.
If a processing job fails, the system shall preserve source data and provide a user-actionable error.
The system shall maintain versioned database migrations with backup-before-migration and rollback guidance.
If a database migration fails, the system shall preserve the pre-migration library and prevent partial normal use.
The system shall verify application and model update signatures before installation.
The system shall support stable, beta, and development release channels.
Where automatic application updates are enabled, the system shall allow postponement during active recording or processing.
If an update fails health checks, the system shall offer rollback to the previous working version.
The system shall publish a supported operating-system, hardware, local model, language, quantization, and optional integration compatibility matrix.

The system shall define and enforce performance budgets for capture CPU, dropped frames, transcript latency, Gemma model loading, local summary latency, local RAG, memory, indexing throughput, search latency, and UI responsiveness.
The system shall measure capture dropped frames and buffer overruns without recording meeting content in telemetry.
The desktop application shall remain responsive to stop and privacy-pause commands under the maximum supported processing load.
The system shall provide progress, cancellation, and estimated work remaining for long-running local processing.
The system shall avoid blocking the primary UI thread with model loading, indexing, export, or integration operations.
The system shall support keyboard-only operation for all core workflows.
The system shall expose semantic names, roles, states, and relationships to screen readers.
The system shall provide sufficient color contrast and shall not use color as the only status indicator.
The system shall support scalable text and layouts without clipping at the defined zoom levels.
The system shall provide captions or transcripts for product tutorial media.
The system shall support light, dark, and system appearance modes.
The system shall provide localization infrastructure that separates UI strings from code.
The system shall support locale-aware dates, times, numbers, names, and first-day-of-week behavior.
The system shall support right-to-left layout for approved locales.
The system shall preserve original spoken language and user-selected output language independently.

The system shall pass an automated zero-egress test for recording, transcription, diarization, Gemma summarization, embedding generation, retrieval, meeting chat, artifact generation, and library search.
The system shall validate TLS certificates for optional connectors and self-hosted synchronization endpoints and shall not provide an unsafe bypass in normal UI.
The system shall protect against path traversal, malicious media, malformed imports, prompt injection, and untrusted connector payloads.
The system shall scan third-party dependencies and local model artifacts for known security, integrity, provenance, and license risks before release.
The system shall maintain a software bill of materials for released application and server packages.
The system shall provide a documented vulnerability reporting and response process.
The system shall support privacy-safe local logs with configurable levels and retention.
The system shall redact secrets and user content from logs by default.
When the user requests support, the system shall allow a diagnostic bundle to be reviewed before submission.
The system shall provide health checks for the local Gemma runtime, transcription runtime, database, media storage, local indexes, model files, optional connectors, and private synchronization.
The system shall maintain automated unit, integration, contract, migration, UI, performance, security, and cross-platform smoke tests.

The system shall use a versioned evaluation corpus to detect local summary, extraction, retrieval, citation, latency, memory, and no-egress regressions.

The system shall expose a documented local extension or plugin interface only through explicit permissions and versioned contracts.

The system shall isolate plugin failure from capture and primary library integrity.
The system shall allow a plugin to be disabled and removed without deleting core meeting data.
The system shall document stable local extension points for approved models, templates, exporters, connectors, and insight rules without exposing an external AI provider interface.
The system shall preserve backward compatibility for published export and webhook schemas according to the documented support policy.
The system shall provide feature flags and safe rollout controls for high-risk capture, AI, synchronization, and integration changes.
The system shall provide release notes that distinguish new, changed, fixed, deprecated, and security-relevant behavior.
The system shall provide an in-product migration and deprecation notice before removing a supported local model, quantization, schema, export format, or workflow.
The system shall meet the defined crash-free session, capture success, processing success, and data-loss service-level objectives before general availability.
The system shall support Local Personal, Encrypted Peer-to-Peer Team, and Self-Hosted Private Team deployment modes and shall not require a managed cloud account.
The system shall allow a user to create or join one or more workspaces.
The system shall support workspace roles for Owner, Administrator, Member, Reviewer, and Guest.
The system shall support group-based permissions and project-level membership.
The system shall enforce authorization before listing, searching, retrieving, generating from, exporting, sharing, or integrating meeting data.
The system shall allow meeting owners to grant read, comment, edit, approve, export, and manage permissions independently.
The system shall support comments, mentions, and threaded discussion on meetings, transcript segments, actions, decisions, and artifacts.
When a user is mentioned, the system shall create a notification that links to the referenced object.
The system shall allow action items to be assigned to workspace members and external email participants.
The system shall allow reviewers to approve or reject artifacts and outbound actions with comments.
The system shall support shared template libraries with versioning and permission controls.
The system shall support shared vocabulary and approved speaker directories scoped by workspace or project.
Before a voice profile is shared across a workspace, the system shall enforce configured consent and policy requirements.
The system shall synchronize approved meetings, edits, tasks, decisions, comments, and configuration through encrypted peer-to-peer or self-hosted channels according to workspace policy.
While a device is offline, the system shall allow permitted local work and queue synchronization operations.
When concurrent edits conflict, the system shall preserve both versions and provide a resolution workflow.
The system shall not silently discard a user edit during synchronization.
Where private team synchronization is enabled, the system shall encrypt eligible content before it leaves the client device.

The system shall keep transcription, summarization, embeddings, retrieval, and meeting chat on authorized client devices; a synchronization server shall not require plaintext access to perform AI processing.
The system shall support OIDC-based single sign-on for team deployments.
The system shall support SCIM-compatible user and group provisioning for enterprise deployments.
The system shall support administrator-enforced MFA, session duration, device, and reauthentication policies where the identity provider supports them.
The system shall provide immutable audit events for authentication, access, edits, exports, shares, policy changes, connector actions, and deletion.
The system shall allow authorized administrators to search and export audit events.
The system shall provide retention policies by workspace, project, meeting type, and content class.
Where legal hold is applied, the system shall preserve covered content and record policy changes.
The system shall support explicit storage-region and infrastructure controls for self-hosted private deployments.
The system shall enforce local-only AI and allow administrators to restrict integration destinations, share links, export formats, model imports, and mobile synchronization.

The system shall provide an administrator view of storage, indexing, processing queues, approved local model usage, synchronization health, connector health, and policy violations without exposing meeting content unnecessarily.
The system shall support workspace backup, restore, and disaster-recovery procedures with integrity verification.
When a user is removed from a workspace, the system shall revoke access tokens and apply the configured ownership-transfer and content-retention policy.
The system shall allow a user to export personal content permitted by workspace policy before offboarding.
The system shall provide signed, versioned, and rollback-capable self-hosted upgrades.
The system shall expose health checks and metrics suitable for self-hosted monitoring without exposing meeting content.
The system shall provide workspace-isolation and authorization tests for self-hosted multi-workspace deployments.
The system shall document feature differences and privacy implications across Local Personal, Encrypted Peer-to-Peer Team, and Self-Hosted Private Team modes.
The system shall support at least one fully local transcription path on every supported desktop platform.

The system shall provide a versioned adapter interface for approved local Whisper, Parakeet, diarization, and user-imported compatible transcription models without exposing external transcription endpoints.
When transcription starts, the system shall record the local model, version, language mode, decoding settings, hardware backend, and local runtime provenance.
While live transcription is enabled, the system shall display provisional text separately from confirmed transcript segments.
When provisional words become stable according to the active decoder policy, the system shall commit them as confirmed segments.
If a provisional hypothesis changes, the system shall update it without creating duplicate confirmed text.
The system shall preserve word- or segment-level timestamps sufficient to navigate from text to media.
The system shall preserve source-track attribution for every transcript segment.
When microphone and system tracks are separate, the system shall label microphone speech as the local participant before full speaker identification.
The system shall support automatic spoken-language detection and explicit user selection.
If automatic language confidence is below the configured threshold, the system shall request confirmation before final processing.
The system shall allow a meeting to contain multiple identified languages and shall preserve the language of each segment.
The system shall allow the summary output language to differ from the spoken language.
The system shall expose model language limitations before a meeting begins.
The system shall allow users to create reusable vocabulary lists for names, organizations, products, acronyms, and domain terminology.
When a meeting is assigned to a project or client, the system shall apply the configured vocabulary hints for that scope.
The system shall allow users to correct transcript text inline while preserving the original machine output in revision history.
When a user corrects a recurring proper noun, the system shall offer to add the correction to the relevant vocabulary scope.
The system shall allow users to select a transcript range and re-transcribe it with a selected model or language.
When a transcript range is reprocessed, the system shall preserve user edits outside the selected range.
When a whole meeting is re-transcribed, the system shall create a new transcript version rather than silently replacing the previous version.
The system shall allow users to compare transcript versions and choose the active version.
The system shall represent diarization speakers independently from named people so labels can be corrected without reprocessing audio.
When diarization completes, the system shall assign every speech segment to a speaker label or explicitly mark it unassigned.
The system shall allow users to rename a diarized speaker and propagate the name across the selected meeting.
When a speaker name is changed, the system shall update dependent summaries, tasks, and decisions only after user approval or explicit regeneration.
The system shall allow users to merge two diarized speakers when one person was split into multiple labels.
The system shall allow users to split incorrectly merged speaker segments and reassign selected segments.
Where speaker memory is enabled, the system shall store voice profiles locally or in the approved workspace boundary.
Before creating a reusable speaker profile, the system shall obtain user confirmation and display the profile scope and deletion controls.
When a known speaker is detected above the confidence threshold, the system shall suggest the identity and allow correction.
If speaker identity confidence is below the threshold, the system shall retain a generic speaker label rather than assert a name.
The system shall allow a speaker profile and its voice embedding to be deleted independently of meeting transcripts.
The system shall not infer sensitive personal attributes from voice.
The system shall distinguish diarization confidence from speech-recognition confidence in data and UI.
The system shall highlight low-confidence transcript words or segments when confidence display is enabled.
When confidence display is disabled, the system shall retain confidence metadata for later review and quality evaluation.
The system shall provide an audio-follow mode that highlights the currently playing transcript segment.
When the user selects a transcript segment, the system shall seek media playback to the corresponding timestamp.
The system shall support search-and-replace across the active transcript with preview and undo.
The system shall prevent overlapping or out-of-order segment edits from corrupting the meeting timeline.
The system shall maintain a transcript revision history including actor, timestamp, and change summary.
If live transcription falls behind the configured latency budget, the system shall display the lag and prioritize catch-up after capture safety.
The system shall provide a per-model benchmark report including measured real-time factor, memory use, language support, and evaluation-set accuracy.
Where custom local transcription models are allowed, the system shall validate model compatibility and isolate model failures from the capture process.

If the selected local transcription model becomes unavailable or fails, the system shall retain the queued job and offer retry, an installed local alternative, Record Only, or deferred local processing.
The system shall support batch transcription of imported audio with progress, cancellation, and resumability.
The system shall preserve a machine-readable alignment between transcript versions and source media.
